candidates.change_summary: Replace the return value with bytes4(0xdeadbeef) to return a different selector.
Replace the return value with bytes4(0) to return zero instead of the expected selector.
Delete the return statement so the function returns the default zero value (0x00000000) instead of the selector.
Replace `baseToken = _baseToken;` with `baseToken = address(0);` so baseToken is always set to zero address regardless of the parameter.
Replace `baseToken = _baseToken;` with `baseToken = address(0xdead);` to assign a hardcoded non-zero address.

Delete the assignment `baseToken = _baseToken;` so baseToken retains its default zero value (or previous value if re-initialization were possible, but since initialized check prevents that, it stays zero).
Replace the assignment `nft = _nft;` with `nft = address(0);` so the state variable is set to zero instead of the provided address.
Delete the line `nft = _nft;` entirely, leaving `nft` uninitialized (defaulting to address(0)).
Replace the assignment `nft = _nft;` with `nft = baseToken;` so `nft` is set to the base token address instead of the provided NFT address.
Replace the assignment `nft = _nft;` with `nft = address(this);` so `nft` is set to the private pool's own address.
Removed the assignment of changeFee from the parameter _changeFee, so changeFee remains the default zero value after initialization.
Assigned changeFee to a hardcoded non-zero value instead of the parameter _changeFee.
Replace the fee rate assignment with a constant value, so the stored feeRate differs from the provided argument after initialize.
Remove the fee rate assignment so feeRate retains its default zero value regardless of the _feeRate argument.
Remove the fee rate upper bound check so that a value above 5000 is stored, bypassing the revert condition.
Swap the fee rate assignment with the changeFee assignment so feeRate gets the value intended for changeFee.
Delete the assignment 'initialized = true;' so the contract is never marked as initialized.
Delete the early return guard 'if (initialized) revert AlreadyInitialized();' so initialize can succeed more than once.
Replace `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` with `payRoyalties = !_payRoyalties;` to invert the stored value.
Replace `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` with `payRoyalties = false;` so it always stores false regardless of input.
Replace `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` with `payRoyalties = true;` so it always stores true regardless of input.
Delete the assignment `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` so the variable retains its default false value.
